title: Humphrey's method and teaching style
summary: The Carl Fischer method book, singing and counting numbers, foot-tapping, and half-hour strict lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I wondered if you remembered anything else about your lessons, any of what method you used on your combo?

Coral fishing. Coral fishing. I think. Anything in particular about his teaching, how he made you count or whether you had to sing the numbers first or anything? What did he have you to do? He had to sing the numbers.
And count. They taught me not the way they teach like this.
Where you slide, you put your, pack your foot down and slide it over for the second beat.
That's the, the banjo player. How do you do? That's the Bill Russell piano.
That's the noise. That's the noise. Now, golf call it. He plays piano, yeah. He still play piano then, I guess. What is your first name?
Gabriel, Clarence Gabriel. Clarence Gabriel. You still play banjo, do you think? I still can play. You can play but you don't have a banjo.
Oh. We like to interview you some of these days too when you have time. We do this with Tulane University trying to get the history of the old time music. All of the jazz musicians that we can find.
You want one of those photographs? Is he on one of those? No. We don't have a photograph with him.
Or the band. You don't have a photograph with a band. We got a different picture to Ruth. You could get it.

When we interview you, maybe we can make a copy of that someday. Is there anything else about Jim Humphrey's teaching that you can remember? You mentioned about the counting and the method. About how long did the lessons last?
The lessons last a half an hour. Was he very strict?
Yeah, he was strict. He was strict.
